newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/HCIA puts soar on stock slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/HCIA puts soar on stock slide.

text.p: Few puts on HCIA Inc traded on Tuesday, but the ones that did trade soared in value as the stock collapsed after the company warned third and fourth quarter profits would likely fall short of expectations.
The HCIA October 55 put, which had open interest of 30, climbed 22-1/4 points to 23. It traded 30 contracts.
The option traded 30 contracts on Monday also.
Similarly, the October 60 put, with open interest of five, traded five contracts Tuesday and Monday. On Tuesday, the option surged to 28 from Monday's 2-3/16 close.
"Somebody taking a profit, it looks like," one trader said.
He said the Monday trades could be suspicious since it appeared the options were bought on Monday just before the earnings shortfall was announced.
Shares of the Baltimore-based health care information services company fell 27-1/8 points to 32-7/8 on turnover of 11.4 million shares.
Late Monday, HCIA said it would not meet its third quarter revenue goals.
Analysts said Tuesday the company would likely need a couple of quarters to recover from the shortfall as management refocused on sales to large customers.
Among the HCIA options, the newly listed October 35 calls drew the most interest, with 423 contracts trading. The option traded between 3/4 and 1-7/8 and closed at its high.
The November 35 put was the next most active, with about 270 contracts changing hands. Also a newly listed option, it traded between 1-3/4 and 3-1/4 before ending at 3-1/4.
The October 40 call traded 172 contracts and the October 45 call traded 143. The December 50 call traded 152.
The two HCIA calls with the highest open interest, the October and November 60s, did not trade.
The trader said the new calls were attracting buyers as investors expected the shares to recover at least some of the ground lost on Tuesday.
The October 60 call, with open interest of 36, closed at 2-11/16. The asking price was 1/16.
The November 60 call had open interest of 40 and was last traded on September 27, when it closed at 3-7/8. The asking price was 1/8. --Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
